question: Should bounded legacy publication fallback retain terminal outcomes in the canonical Cloudflare state layer, and what durable revision-fence semantics should apply after detailed terminal metadata is compacted?
rationale: The current branch’s controller-local ledger is mechanically incompatible with the architecture merged after its base, and choosing the permanent terminal-state authority is a product and persistence-contract decision rather than a rebase-only repair.

options.title: Canonicalize fallback terminal state
options.body: Replace the controller-local ledger with canonical-state-backed terminal semantics for the remaining legacy fallback, including explicit retention and revision-fence behavior.

options.title: Retire the fallback first
options.body: Remove or further constrain the legacy fallback before adding any new terminal persistence, if its remaining operational value no longer warrants another durable contract.

recommendation.title: Canonicalize fallback terminal state
recommendation.body: Replace the controller-local ledger with canonical-state-backed terminal semantics for the remaining legacy fallback, including explicit retention and revision-fence behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The current direct-publication and Cloudflare-canonical persistence boundary was introduced through the recent merged work associated with this area.
